producer_report.summary: When `planning_round` raises the planner's effort on a revision call (round above 1 or a mechanical revision), the planner time limit is now `planner_timeout_s` times a new constant `PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` (2, so 1200 s from 600 s), using `saturating_mul`. Escalation is detected by comparing the effort `planner_revision_setting` returns with the planner's own. That function returns the effort unchanged unless the key is set and stronger, so round 1, a seeded first call, and an unset, weaker or equal key keep exactly `planner_timeout_s`. The root cause was that every planner call got the base limit, including a call raised to xhigh, as in job 20261114-041123-hvyh (606 s against 600 s). The critic limit, `planner_usd` and the config keys are unchanged. The tests record `spec.timeout` in the `run_for_revision` fixture, and four new tests cover the scaled and unscaled cases. CHANGELOG.md has a Fixed entry.

criteria_check.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs configures planner_revision_effort higher than the planner's effort with planner_timeout_s = 600, runs a revision round (round 2), and asserts the planner AgentSpec timeout is greater than 600 s. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria_check.evidence: New test a_stronger_revision_effort_scales_the_planner_time_limit uses repo_with_revision_keys(3, SONNET, "xhigh") (planner_timeout_s = 600, planner effort high) and a critic revise. It asserts planner limits are [600 s, >600 s] and equal to 1200 s. It passed in cargo test -p athena-core planner_ and in the full cargo test -p athena-core --lib.

criteria_check.criterion: A test asserts that round 1 and a revision without escalated effort (no planner_revision_effort set, or not stronger) still use exactly planner_timeout_s. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria_check.evidence: New tests: planner_time_limit_is_unscaled_when_no_revision_key_is_set (3 calls, all exactly 600 s); planner_time_limit_is_unscaled_when_the_revision_effort_is_not_stronger (weaker keys, and effort key equal to high: all 600 s); planner_time_limit_is_unscaled_in_round_1_and_scaled_on_the_mechanical_revision (first call 600 s, mechanical revision 1200 s). All passed.

criteria_check.criterion: The diff in crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs scales cfg.planner_timeout_s only when the revision setting raises effort, via a named constant with a doc comment saying why (job 20261114-041123-hvyh hit 600 s at xhigh).
criteria_check.evidence: git diff of planning.rs: const PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR: u64 = 2 with a doc comment citing job 20261114-041123-hvyh (606 s at xhigh against the 600 s limit). planning_round keeps base_effort and uses saturating_mul only when effort != base_effort after planner_revision_setting; else cfg.planner_timeout_s.

criteria_check.criterion: The deliverables are only planning.rs, run/tests.rs and CHANGELOG.md; athena.toml, defaults.toml, hestia.rs, the prompts and records/ are unchanged in the diff.
criteria_check.evidence: git diff --stat lists only CHANGELOG.md, crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs.

criteria_check.evidence: A new first bullet under [Unreleased] / Fixed gives the root cause, cites job 20261114-041123-hvyh (round 2, xhigh, 606 s, 600 s deadline) and the 2x fix. It also says the 2x is an estimate and names the tests.

open_issues: docs/decisions.md D179 still says planner_timeout_s is unchanged on the revision call. I did not edit docs/decisions.md or config.rs, to keep to criterion 4. The CHANGELOG entry records that this is superseded. A follow-up decision entry could be added if wanted.
The 2x factor is an estimate from one 606 s observation; 1200 s may still be too short or longer than needed.
mistakes: I first tried a heredoc and piped commands; the hook denied them and I redid the work with the Edit tool and plain cargo commands.
learnings: planner_revision_setting returns the effort string unchanged unless the key is set and stronger, so comparing strings detects escalation.
The test seam run_for_revision reads AgentInvocation.timeout directly from the fake script closure.
Bash in this environment denies pipes, grep, tail and here-documents.
desires: Pipes and here-documents are denied for the producer role; a way to read long cargo output would help.
